questions.question:
The marks obtained by the students of a class are given. Find the standard deviation of the marks (rounded off to 2 decimal places).

 65, 47, 59, 75, 82, 91, 55 and 78
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Find the **Mean (μ)** of the marks: (65 + 47 + 59 + 75 + 82 + 91 + 55 + 78) ÷ 8 = 552 ÷ 8 = **69**.

Calculate the sum of squared deviations from the mean: 16 + 484 + 100 + 36 + 169 + 484 + 196 + 81 = **1566**.

Find the **Variance (σ²)**: 1566 ÷ 8 = **195.75**.

Calculate the **Standard Deviation (σ)**: √195.75 ≈ **13.99**.

**∴ The correct answer is 13.99.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Marks obtained by students: 65, 47, 59, 75, 82, 91, 55, 78

Total number of students (N) = 8

questions.question:
If the mode of the following data is 165, then what is the value of x?

 
 

 Class
 150-155
 155-160
 160-165
 165-170
 170-175
 
 
 
 

 Frequency
 13
 26
 37
 x
 27
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When the **Mode** of a distribution is equal to the **Upper Limit** of a class interval, the frequency of that class (f₁) must be equal to the frequency of the succeeding class (f₂).

Given **Mode** = 165, which is the upper limit of the class **160−165**.

Frequency of class (160−165) = 37.

Frequency of the next class (165−170) = x.

∴ **x = 37**.

**∴ The correct answer is 37.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Mode** = 165

Since 165 lies at the boundary of 160−165 and 165−170, we identify the **Modal Class** as 160−165.

Lower limit (l) = 160

Frequency of modal class (f₁) = 37

Frequency of preceding class (f₀) = 26

Frequency of succeeding class (f₂) = x

Class width (h) = 5

**Formula:**

Mode = l + [(f₁ − f₀) ÷ (2f₁ − f₀ − f₂)] × h

**Calculations:**

⇒ 165 = 160 + [(37 − 26) ÷ (2 × 37 − 26 − x)] × 5

⇒ 165 − 160 = [11 ÷ (74 − 26 − x)] × 5

⇒ 5 = [11 ÷ (48 − x)] × 5

⇒ 1 = 11 ÷ (48 − x)

⇒ 48 − x = 11

⇒ x = 48 − 11

⇒ x = 37

**∴ The correct answer is 37.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Empirical Relationship

The relationship between the three measures of central tendency is: **Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean**.

Median of Grouped Data

Median = l + [((n ÷ 2) − cf) ÷ f] × h, where **cf** is the cumulative frequency of the class preceding the median class.

Mean of Grouped Data

Mean (μ) = Σ(fᵢ × xᵢ) ÷ Σfᵢ, where **xᵢ** is the class mark (mid-point) of each interval.</p

questions.question: The mode of the observations 9, 6, 4, 2, 5, 2, 9, 2, 1, 9, 4, 5, 9, 5, 4 and 8 is:
questions.solution:

Count the occurrences of each number in the given **observations**.

Frequency of 9 = 4 times.

Frequency of 2, 4, and 5 = 3 times each.

Since 9 has the **maximum frequency**, it is the mode.

**∴ The correct answer is 9.**

questions.question: If the mode of a data set exceeds its mean by 37.8, then the mode exceeds the median by _____. (Use empirical formula.)
questions.solution: __Shortcut Trick__ The relationship between **Mean**, **Median**, and **Mode** is defined by the ratio of their differences. Using the empirical formula: (Mode − Median) = 2/3 × (Mode − Mean) Given: (Mode − Mean) = 37.8 Calculation: (Mode − Median) = 2/3 × 37.8 = 2 × 12.6 = 25.2 **∴ The correct answer is 25.2.** **__Alternate Method__** Given: **Mode − Mean = 37.8** Formula Used: **Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0923f82fe7e6a865f7c25b10254933ed1abf42639f8e9e7e5198370226e65562.png] ⇒ Mode − Mean = 37.8 ⇒ Mean = Mode − 37.8 ⇒ Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × (Mode − 37.8) ⇒ Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mode + 75.6 ⇒ 3 × Mode − 3 × Median = 75.6 ⇒ 3(Mode − Median) = 75.6 ⇒ Mode − Median = 75.6 ÷ 3 = 25.2 **∴ The correct answer is 25.2.** **__Additional Information__**

questions.question:
What is the median of the following data?

13, 43, 81, 27, 25, 28, 87, 57, 77, 89, 73
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Arrange the **data** in **ascending order**: 13, 25, 27, 28, 43, 57, 73, 77, 81, 87, 89.

Count the total number of terms (n) = 11 (which is an **odd number**).

The **median** is the middle-most term, which is the ((11 + 1) ÷ 2) = 6th term.

The 6th term in the sorted sequence is 57.

**∴ The correct answer is 57.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Data set = {13, 43, 81, 27, 25, 28, 87, 57, 77, 89, 73}

**Formula Used:** Median = ((n + 1) ÷ 2)th term, where n is the **number of observations** (when n is odd).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9dbd7d861420095682e6f8e03e83adf2080230f5bcbebbc27360328e6bf7b31d.png] 

⇒ Arrange the observations in **ascending order**: 13, 25, 27, 28, 43, 57, 73, 77, 81, 87, 89

⇒ Total number of observations (n) = 11

⇒ Median = ((11 + 1) ÷ 2)th observation

⇒ Median = 6th observation

⇒ Median = 57

**∴ The correct answer is 57.**

**__Additional Information__**

Median for Even Number of Terms

If the number of observations (n) is **even**, the median is the average of the (n ÷ 2)th and ((n ÷ 2) + 1)th terms.

Arithmetic Mean

The **mean** is the sum of all observations divided by the total number of observations (Sum ÷ n).

Mode

The **mode** is the value that occurs most frequently in a data set. A data set can be unimodal, bimodal, or multimodal.</p

Let the **assumed mean (A)** be 22.

Calculate deviations (dᵢ = xᵢ − 22):

∑fᵢdᵢ = 98×(−10) + 74×0 + 17×36 + 28×57 + 44×67 = −980 + 0 + 612 + 1596 + 2948 = 4176

Total frequency (N) = 98 + 74 + 17 + 28 + 44 = 261

Actual Mean = A + (∑fᵢdᵢ ÷ N) = 22 + (4176 ÷ 261) = 22 + 16 = 38

**∴ The correct answer is 38.**

questions.question:
What is the median of the following distribution?

 
 

 Class
 150-200
 200-250
 250-300
 300-350
 350-400
 
 
 
 

 Frequency
 20
 19
 32
 27
 12
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Total Frequency **N** = 110, so **N/2** = 55.

Cumulative Frequencies are: 20, 39, **71**, 98, 110.

The value 55 falls in the **250−300** class (Median Class).

Median = 250 + [(55 − 39) ÷ 32] × 50 = 250 + [16 ÷ 32] × 50 = 250 + 25 = 275.

**∴ The correct answer is 275.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Frequency distribution for classes 150−400.

**Formula Used:** Median = L + [((N/2) − cf) ÷ f] × h

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/05d38459f86d3edb1b9a1949910a228fb68c42158a7504f99b025e3477beb6db.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total frequency **N** = 20 + 19 + 32 + 27 + 12 = 110

⇒ **N/2** = 110 ÷ 2 = 55

⇒ Cumulative Frequencies (CF): 20, 39, 71, 98, 110

⇒ Since 55 lies in the cumulative frequency 71, **Median Class** = 250−300

⇒ Lower limit **L** = 250, Frequency **f** = 32, Prev CF **cf** = 39, Class width **h** = 50

⇒ Median = 250 + [(55 − 39) ÷ 32] × 50

⇒ Median = 250 + [16 ÷ 32] × 50

⇒ Median = 250 + 0.5 × 50 = 250 + 25 = 275

**∴ The correct answer is 275.**

**__Additional Information__**

Median of Grouped Data

The median is the middle value of a data set. For grouped data, it is calculated using the formula: Median = L + [((N/2) − cf) / f] × h.

Empirical Relationship

For a moderately skewed distribution: **Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean**.

Median Class Identification

The median class is the first class interval whose **cumulative frequency** is greater than or equal to **N/2**.</p

questions.question: If the mode of a data exceeds its mean by 20.1, then the mode exceeds the median by _____. (Use empirical formula)
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Use the direct relationship derived from the **Empirical Formula**: **(Mode − Median) = 2/3 × (Mode − Mean)**.

Given that **Mode − Mean = 20.1**.

Substitute the value: **Mode − Median = 2/3 × 20.1**.

Calculation: **2 × 6.7 = 13.4**.

**∴ The correct answer is 13.4.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The difference between **Mode** and **Mean** = 20.1

**Formula Used:**

The **Empirical Relationship** between central tendencies is: **Mode = 3 Median − 2 Mean**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8f916c8502cd9b2f76988743b9c13d888f5a228e8a86789c05b0446008058089.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Mode − Mean = 20.1**

⇒ **Mean = Mode − 20.1**

⇒ Using **Mode = 3 Median − 2 Mean**

⇒ Mode = 3 Median − 2 (Mode − 20.1)

⇒ Mode = 3 Median − 2 Mode + 40.2

⇒ Mode + 2 Mode − 3 Median = 40.2

⇒ 3 Mode − 3 Median = 40.2

⇒ 3 (Mode − Median) = 40.2

⇒ Mode − Median = 40.2 ÷ 3

⇒ **Mode − Median = 13.4**

**∴ The correct answer is 13.4.**

**__Additional Information__**

Empirical Formula

The relationship **Mode = 3 Median − 2 Mean** is valid for moderately skewed distributions.

Symmetric Distribution

In a perfectly **symmetrical distribution**, the values of Mean, Median, and Mode coincide (**Mean = Median = Mode**).

Skewness and Central Tendency

In a **negatively skewed** distribution, Mean < Median < Mode. In a **positively skewed** distribution, Mode < Median < Mean.</p

questions.question:
What is the median of the following data?

72, 47, 98, 52, 20, 86, 85, 69, 59, 81, 53
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Arrange the given data in **ascending order**: 20, 47, 52, 53, 59, 69, 72, 81, 85, 86, 98.

Count of observations (N) = 11 (which is an **odd number**).

**Median** = ((N + 1) ÷ 2)th term = (12 ÷ 2)th term = **6th term**.

The 6th term in the sorted sequence is **69**.

**∴ The correct answer is 69.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Data set: 72, 47, 98, 52, 20, 86, 85, 69, 59, 81, 53

Total number of observations (N) = **11**

**Formula Used:**

When N is odd, **Median** = ((N + 1) ÷ 2)th observation.

When N is even, **Median** = [ (N ÷ 2)th observation + ((N ÷ 2) + 1)th observation ] ÷ 2.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5819b9a4cd9df52c6b63eac150d4efc7f7e692a8c5ee8a8be7a238be204256de.png] 

**Calculations:**

First, arrange the data in ascending order:

⇒ 20, 47, 52, 53, 59, 69, 72, 81, 85, 86, 98

Since N = 11 (which is an odd number):

⇒ Median = ((11 + 1) ÷ 2)th term

⇒ Median = 6th term

⇒ The 6th term in the sorted list is **69**.

Let us analyze why the other options are incorrect:

⇒ **Option (1) 68.5** is incorrect because it is not the middle value of the sorted dataset.

⇒ **Option (2) 70** is incorrect because 70 is not present in the dataset and is not the median.

⇒ **Option (4) 69.5** is incorrect because it would be the median if the number of terms was even and the two middle terms averaged to 69.5, which is not the case here.

**∴ The correct answer is 69.**

**__Additional Information__**

Median for Even Number of Terms

If the number of observations (N) is even, the median is the average of the (N ÷ 2)th and ((N ÷ 2) + 1)th terms after sorting.

Relation between Mean, Median, and Mode

For a moderately skewed distribution, the empirical relationship is: Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean.

Properties of Median

The median is not affected by extreme values (outliers) in the dataset, making it a more robust measure of central tendency than the mean for skewed distributions.</p

questions.question: If the median of a data is 45.98 less than its mode, then the median of the data exceeds its mean by _____. (Use empirical formula)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **Empirical Relationship** between central tendencies is: **(Mode − Median) = 2 × (Median − Mean)**.

Given that **Median** is 45.98 less than **Mode**, we have: **Mode − Median = 45.98**.

Applying the trick: 45.98 = 2 × (Median − Mean).

Required value = 45.98 ÷ 2 = 22.99.

**∴ The correct answer is 22.99.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Difference between **Mode** and **Median** = 45.98

**Formula Used:**

**Empirical Formula:** Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0844e395c8720a7ca75b75b6d324ae49949ecfc5c16cad7b5727a88cda9b31f8.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean

Subtract **Median** from both sides:

⇒ Mode − Median = (3 × Median − 2 × Mean) − Median

⇒ Mode − Median = 2 × Median − 2 × Mean

⇒ Mode − Median = 2 × (Median − Mean)

Substitute the given value (Mode − Median = 45.98):

⇒ 45.98 = 2 × (Median − Mean)

⇒ Median − Mean = 45.98 ÷ 2

⇒ Median − Mean = 22.99

**∴ The correct answer is 22.99.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Empirical Relationship

For a moderately skewed distribution, the relationship is **Mode = 3 Median − 2 Mean**. This is also expressed as **Mean − Mode = 3(Mean − Median)**.

Symmetrical Distribution

In a perfectly **symmetrical distribution** (like a Normal Distribution), the values of **Mean**, **Median**, and **Mode** are all equal (Mean = Median = Mode).

Skewness and Central Tendency

In a **positively skewed** distribution, Mean > Median > Mode. In a **negatively skewed** distribution, Mode > Median > Mean.</p

questions.question:
What is the median of the following data?

61, 55, 18, 49, 52, 80, 60, 33, 54, 56, 28
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Arrange the given data in **ascending order**:

18, 28, 33, 49, 52, **54**, 55, 56, 60, 61, 80

Total number of observations (n) = 11 (which is an **odd number**).

Median = ((n + 1) ÷ 2)th term = (12 ÷ 2)th term = 6th term = 54

**∴ The correct answer is 54.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The dataset is: 61, 55, 18, 49, 52, 80, 60, 33, 54, 56, 28

**Formula Used:**

To find the **median** of a dataset:

1. Arrange the data in ascending or descending order.

2. If the number of observations (n) is **odd**:

Median = ((n + 1) ÷ 2)th observation

3. If the number of observations (n) is **even**:

Median = [ (n ÷ 2)th observation + ((n ÷ 2) + 1)th observation ] ÷ 2

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1335031cc111c1176a89e3ef49e4e86eb97aec064268bafe2652b92de38929c3.png] 

**Calculations:**

Arrange the given observations in ascending order:

⇒ 18, 28, 33, 49, 52, 54, 55, 56, 60, 61, 80

Count the total number of observations (n):

⇒ n = 11

Since n is odd, we use the odd formula for median:

⇒ Median = ((11 + 1) ÷ 2)th term

⇒ Median = (12 ÷ 2)th term

⇒ Median = 6th term

Looking at the arranged data, the 6th term is 54.

⇒ Median = 54

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Calculate **Total Frequency (N)** = 14 + 37 + 28 + 39 + 12 = 130.

Find **N/2** = 130 ÷ 2 = 65.

Identify **Median Class** by **Cumulative Frequency (CF)**: 14, 51, 79... (65 falls in the 240-290 class).

Apply **Median** = L + [(N/2 − CFₚ) ÷ f] × h = 240 + [(65 − 51) ÷ 28] × 50.

Median = 240 + [14 ÷ 28] × 50 = 240 + 25 = 265.

**∴ The correct answer is 265.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Distribution of classes and their respective frequencies.

**Formula Used:** Median = L + [((N/2) − CF) ÷ f] × h

Where: **L** = Lower limit of median class, **N** = Total frequency, **CF** = Cumulative frequency of preceding class, **f** = Frequency of median class, **h** = Class width.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/24a454f96db51d6b958ebef11129573311481b7b76dd22ee1bba3b5da362631e.png] 

**Step 1: Calculate Cumulative Frequencies (CF)**

⇒ Class 140-190: f = 14, CF = 14

⇒ Class 190-240: f = 37, CF = 14 + 37 = 51

⇒ Class 240-290: f = 28, CF = 51 + 28 = 79

⇒ Class 290-340: f = 39, CF = 79 + 39 = 118

⇒ Class 340-390: f = 12, CF = 118 + 12 = 130

**Step 2: Find Median Class**

⇒ Total Frequency (N) = 130

⇒ N/2 = 130 ÷ 2 = 65

⇒ The CF just greater than 65 is 79, which corresponds to the **Median Class 240-290**.

**Step 3: Apply Median Formula**

⇒ L = 240, CF = 51, f = 28, h = 50

⇒ Median = 240 + [(65 − 51) ÷ 28] × 50

⇒ Median = 240 + [14 ÷ 28] × 50

⇒ Median = 240 + [0.5 × 50]

⇒ Median = 240 + 25 = 265

**∴ The correct answer is 265.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Empirical Relationship

For a moderately skewed distribution: **Mode = 3 Median − 2 Mean**.

Mode of Grouped Data

Mode = L + [(f₁ − f₀) ÷ (2f₁ − f₀ − f₂)] × h, where f₁ is the frequency of the modal class.

Mean of Grouped Data

Mean (μ) = Σ(fᵢ × xᵢ) ÷ Σfᵢ, where xᵢ is the class mark (mid-point) of each interval.</p
